overview.headline: How air density, speed, shape and area create aerodynamic drag

keyPoints.point: Drag grows with air density and with velocity squared plus shape and flow effects
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility

keyPoints.point: Drag equals coefficient times density times speed pressure and area effects
keyPoints.quote: drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ)

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficient bundles form drag plus friction and wave with induced effects
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficients are measured experimentally using wind tunnel testing
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyTerms.gloss: Variable that collects complex shape and flow effects for drag
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: Area chosen to characterize size dependence in drag calculation
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: Combined density and velocity effect that appears in pressure relations
keyTerms.quote: is called the dynamic pressure and appears in Bernoulli’s pressure equation.

keyTerms.gloss: Air mass per volume symbolized by Greek rho in drag relation
keyTerms.quote: In many textbooks on aerodynamics, density is also given by the Greek symbol rho (ρ) (Greek for “r”).

analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers drag dependence on air and shape, drag coefficient meaning, reference area choices, and density and dynamic pressure ideas
